summary: MaterialDNA capacity mining found a byte-size false-bound inside the already proposed HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-DENSE-BOUNDS defect class. validateKnownFields() currently appends the complete caller-supplied unknown string field name into the error text. Even if the proposed cardinality fix stops after a bounded number of unknown keys, one arbitrarily large unknown string key can still force caller-sized diagnostic allocation/copy work before any project-key value validation occurs. Absorb this into the existing dense-bounds lane rather than creating another MaterialDNA lane: unknown-field diagnostics must have a deterministic bounded byte representation (for example bounded prefix/length metadata), preserve useful affected-record/path context, and add a huge-single-key adversary in addition to many-key coverage.
evidence: Retained MaterialDNA counter head #353 (10559afdce1a1854e7932522f6e78561736c8ed3) defines MAX_KEY_LENGTH=160 for canonical project-key values, but closed-record field-name validation occurs separately in validateKnownFields().

validateKnownFields() iterates caller-supplied record keys and formats an unknown string key directly into `{path} contains unknown field {key}` with no byte ceiling or truncation before appendError().

HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-DENSE-BOUNDS already owns unbounded closed-record scan count and per-key diagnostic growth, so this is the same bounded-diagnostics surface and should be absorbed there rather than spawning duplicate WIP.

The existing dense-bounds acceptance can stop after a finite number of invalid keys yet still remain memory-unbounded if the retained diagnostic echoes an arbitrarily large first string key; explicit byte-bounded diagnostic formatting plus a huge-single-key regression closes that false pass.
No product bytes were changed and no Studio/engine evidence is claimed.
